Incorporating the contemporaneous Beige Book (early September 2020) alongside SLOOS refines the assessment. The Beige Book reports modest to moderate increases in activity across most Districts, with notable strength in housing (particularly single-family and refinancing), improving auto sales, and a pickup in manufacturing. However, overall activity and employment remained below pre-pandemic levels; leisure and hospitality, travel, and energy were still weak; commercial real estate—especially retail and lodging—was soft; and uncertainty stayed elevated. Price and wage pressures were generally subdued. Credit demand was mixed, and banks continued to tighten lending standards—consistent with SLOOS—suggesting the bank credit channel would remain a drag even as market functioning improved.

Implication for the FOMC statement: The Beige Book supports the Committee’s cautious, accommodative stance and the emphasis on downside risks and subdued inflation. Compared with an assessment anchored only in market functioning (and SLOOS), Beige Book evidence of broader real-economy healing tempers the negativity somewhat, while still acknowledging significant headwinds from weak services, CRE, and tight bank credit.

Net: Slightly less negative than the SLOOS-only view, but still cautious given uneven recovery and elevated uncertainty.
